title: Role of Artificial Intelligence in Predicting Outcomes of Clinical Trials in Oncology

model.params_source: assumed (the paper states no decoding parameters); max_tokens is small because the prompt asks for a single word

task.subset_rule: the 712 oncology-specific trials of the extracted cohort (2,163 trials in total)
task.approximation: The cohort is defined only by inclusion criteria (interventional oncology trials, Phases I-III, completed with results posted between January 2015 and December 2023, clearly defined primary outcomes, human subjects); no NCT list is published. The Success/Failure labels were assigned by the authors ('NLP-assisted manual review by two clinical experts') and are not published either. Table 1 is captioned 'Overall AI Model Performance' and the text calls it 'the overall predictive accuracy across all clinical trial data', so it may cover the 2,163-trial cohort rather than the 712 oncology trials.

items.source: ClinicalTrials.gov (https://clinicaltrials.gov/api/v2/studies); the authors' curated cohort and its labels are not released
items.config_or_split: interventional oncology trials, Phases I-III, completed 2015-2023 with posted results
items.filter: phase in ['PHASE1','PHASE2','PHASE3'] and overallStatus == 'COMPLETED' and hasResults

fields.input: briefTitle + briefSummary + condition + phase + intervention + primaryOutcome + sponsorType + duration
fields.label: outcome

checks_2026_09_19: ClinicalTrials.gov API v2 answers with HTTP 200 and returns study records carrying the needed fields

prompt.user_template:
Use the following clinical trial data to predict whether the outcome will be a success or failure. Reply with only one word: success or failure.
{trial_data}

placeholders.trial_data: the structured trial record: trial title, summary, disease category, phase, intervention, endpoint type, sponsor type and trial duration (Sec. 'Model Input and Prediction Process')

prompt.source_location: Sec. 'Model Input and Prediction Process' ('Each model was prompted with structured trial data using a standardized instruction')
prompt.verbatim: partial: the instruction sentence is printed verbatim, but the paper does not show how the eight input fields are laid out after it, so the {trial_data} block would be our own serialisation

metric.name: custom
metric.definition: balanced accuracy = (sensitivity + specificity) / 2 over the Success/Failure labels; the runner has no balanced-accuracy metric, so a hook score() would be needed
metric.original_location: Table 1, row GPT-4 (MCC 0.234, Recall 1.000, Specificity 0.083 in the same row)

open_points: Neither the 712-trial cohort (no NCT identifiers) nor the expert Success/Failure labels are published; rebuilding both from ClinicalTrials.gov would produce our own dataset, not the paper's.

It is unclear whether Table 1 covers the 712 oncology trials or all 2,163 extracted trials; either way the row's recall of 1.000 with specificity 0.083 says the model answered 'success' for almost every trial.
The layout of the eight input fields inside the prompt is not printed.
Metric gap: balanced accuracy is not one of the runner's metric names.
notes: The paper's GPT-4o row uses the rolling alias chatgpt-4o-latest and is therefore not reproducible at all; gpt-4-turbo-2024-04-09 is the only dated snapshot in the model table. est_calls assumes 712 trials x 3 seeds.
